correctness.rationale: The monomial coefficient matrix is b_{nk}=(n+1)/(n+k+1)*sqrt(w_n(beta)/w_k(alpha)). In compact range -1<alpha<0,beta>alpha+2, the head k<2^L can be approximated by L geometric terms on each of L dyadic input columns; ratio |c_j-k|/(n+c_j+1) ≤1/3, with one extra exact k=0 column, yielding rank≤1+L². Gamma-ratio weighted column estimates summed across k≥2^L give squared Hilbert–Schmidt tail ≤C(L+1)2^-τL for τ=min(beta-alpha-2,-alpha)>0. Thus norm error ≤C(3^-L+sqrt(L+1)2^-τL/2) and s_N≤C exp(-c sqrt N), hence S_p all p>0. The proof uses infinite tail estimates; inspected source exact rational finite checker only corroborates kernel identities and limited samples. Converse uses earlier Li–Zhou compactness theorem.
